mcqs.question: Which function is nowhere complex-differentiable?
mcqs.explanation: f(z)=z-bar has u=x, v=-y, giving u_x=1 but v_y=-1 — the Cauchy-Riemann equations fail everywhere.

mcqs.question: For a simple closed contour C with z0 OUTSIDE C, and f analytic inside/on C, what is (1/2πi)⌆_C f(z)/(z-z0) dz?
mcqs.explanation: If z0 is outside C, f(z)/(z-z0) is analytic everywhere inside C, so by Cauchy's Theorem the integral is 0.

whyOthersWrong.A: This is the answer only when z0 is INSIDE C.
whyOthersWrong.C: This equals the integral itself when z0 is inside, not the coefficient-normalized version outside.
whyOthersWrong.D: The integral is perfectly well-defined and evaluates to 0.

mcqs.question: Satisfying the Cauchy-Riemann equations at a single isolated point guarantees differentiability there:

options.C: Only if the partial derivatives are also continuous nearby

mcqs.explanation: The converse direction of the Cauchy-Riemann theorem requires continuity of the partial derivatives near the point, not just satisfaction of the equations at that one point.

whyOthersWrong.A: False — see the standard counterexample on the Analytic Functions topic page.
whyOthersWrong.B: Too strong — it can happen, just not automatically.
whyOthersWrong.D: The condition is about continuity of partials, unrelated to whether f is a polynomial.
